entries: Grading and determination | standards and dimensions | Grade and sort unprocessed agricultural products by factors such as colour, variety, length, width, appearance, feel, smell and quality, judging against grade standards and limits and leaving a trace.

Sorting and removal | defects and foreign items | Remove substandard, defective and foreign items, pick out conforming products and isolate, label and register nonconforming ones to prevent batch mixing.
Weighing and measuring | visual and instruments | Weigh or estimate the weight of products visually or by feel, check weight and quantity with measuring equipment and register the results.

Containers and marking | grades and numbers | Pack products into containers by grade as required and mark the grade on the container, and register labels or receipt, issue and sales documents by grade or identification number.
Records and traceability | batches and isolation | Record grade, quantity, batch, isolation and handling information and keep batches and records traceable in support of review and traceability.

Hygiene and process coordination | cleaning and pace | Work to cleaning, foreign item control, temperature and time limit requirements, coordinate with upstream and downstream processes and equipment pace, and report anomalies.

paragraphs: Conclusion | the core difference between this page (O*NET 45-2041.00, Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products) and adjacent roles lies in the object, outputs and authorization level: this occupation takes unprocessed agricultural products, grade standards, metrology and marking as its object, and its outputs are batches judged conforming together with grading, measurement and marking and traceability records; Food Batchmakers (51-3092.00) take batching, mixing and batch making processes as their object; Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers (51-3022.00) take cutting, trimming and boning of meat, poultry and seafood; Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders (51-9111.00) take machine packaging and filling operation; Packers and Packagers, Hand (53-7064.00) take manual packing and boxing; and Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse (45-2092.00) take planting, harvesting and field work. The object, process and authorization level all differ, and the authority to interpret grade standards, accept concessions, release products or certify inspection cannot be carried across roles.

Each occupation's wages and employment must be checked separately against its own SOC measure; this table makes no numerical comparison and does not use one occupation's wage as a proxy for another; hygiene, marking and traceability requirements must be checked against each jurisdiction and institution. The US wages and employment on this page use this occupation's own (45-2041.00) measure presented by O*NET on the 45-2041.00 page (that page does not note that it is taken from a parent occupation) and do not borrow adjacent occupations' values.

Preface | the comparison below is laid out in four columns: occupation direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice fits better. Grading, making, cutting, packing and field work often connect within the same agricultural product or food supply chain, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, the materials, processes, hygiene, qualifications and responsibility boundaries of that direction must be learned anew.

The work objects differ but tasks may overlap: the 45-2092 farmworker definition also includes cleaning, grading, sorting, packing and loading harvested produce, so classification is not exclusive on whether sorting is done. Food batchmakers set up and run mixing and blending equipment, packaging machine roles cover industrial and consumer products of all kinds, and the weighing and recording role is mainly clerical. Authority is checked against the real institutional arrangement.

Better suited to people who are willing to make continuous visual and tactile determinations to grade standards at a grading table or production line, can stay steady and attentive under repetitive motion and pace pressure, and leave a trace in line with hygiene, marking and traceability requirements.

Core work and outputs: check the arrival, batch and specification, sample according to the sampling rules and grade, sort and remove by factors such as colour, variety, length, width, appearance, feel, smell and quality, weigh visually or by feel and check against measuring equipment, pack into containers by grade and mark the grade and identification number on the container and documents, and record grade, quantity, batch, isolation and handling information; the outputs are batches judged conforming together with grading, measurement and marking and traceability records (O*NET/SOC 45-2041.00).

subject.name: Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products
subject.summary: The precise occupation 45-2041.00 handles unprocessed food and other agricultural products, not only edible fruit and vegetables. 5 tasks: 4 core, namely placing products into containers and marking grades by grade 90, weighing or estimating weight visually or by feel 88, removing inferior, defective or foreign items 86, and grading and sorting by colour, variety, size, appearance, feel, smell and quality 86; the supplementary task is recording grades and identification numbers 80. Importance is not an adoption rate or legal authority, and sampling and hygiene are editorial process checking suggestions rather than added official core tasks. 2025 US national wages for this occupation 45-2041: the 10th/25th/50th/75th/90th percentile annual wages are 29,580/34,320/35,730/38,260/44,490 USD, with hourly wages of 14.22/16.50/17.18/18.39/21.39 USD. OEWS includes production bonuses and commissions and excludes non-production bonuses, overtime premiums, shift differentials, benefits and self-employment; national percentiles do not equal starting pay, seniority or an individual's piece-rate peak and off-season earnings. The current US projection is a 3.4% decline over 2025—2035, from 45.4 to 43.8 thousand; the detailed measure is in the body text, and the parent farmworker or adjacent OOH figures are not substituted.
